# Batch mode: encrypt a directory, resume after interruption, and decrypt it.
mkdir -p in/sub/deep
cp key.txt in/a.txt
cp key.txt in/sub/b.txt
cp key.txt in/sub/deep/c.txt

# Normal batch encryption mirrors the directory structure.
age --batch -e -R recipients.txt -o enc in
exists enc/a.txt.age
exists enc/sub/b.txt.age
exists enc/sub/deep/c.txt.age
exists enc/.age-batch-state.json
stderr 'batch summary'
! stderr '1 failed'

# Rerunning is idempotent: everything is skipped, outputs are not rewritten.
cp enc/a.txt.age before-rerun.age
age --batch -e -R recipients.txt -o enc in
stderr '3 skipped'
cmp enc/a.txt.age before-rerun.age

# An untracked pre-existing output is refused, not overwritten.
mkdir -p enc2
cp planted.age enc2/a.txt.age
! age --batch -e -R recipients.txt -o enc2 in
stderr 'already exists'
cmp enc2/a.txt.age planted.age

# Batch decryption restores the full tree, which then matches the input.
age --batch -d -i key.txt -o dec enc
! stderr '1 failed'
cmp dec/a.txt in/a.txt
cmp dec/sub/b.txt in/sub/b.txt
cmp dec/sub/deep/c.txt in/sub/deep/c.txt

# A fresh one-shot run into another directory produces identical plaintexts
# after decryption: resumed/rerun artifacts are equivalent to a clean run.
age --batch -e -R recipients.txt -o enc3 in
age --batch -d -i key.txt -o dec3 enc3
cmp dec3/a.txt in/a.txt
cmp dec3/sub/deep/c.txt in/sub/deep/c.txt

# Startup checks: missing key, passphrase rejection, same input/output dir.
! age --batch -e -R does-not-exist.txt -o enc4 in
stderr 'failed to open recipient file'
! age --batch -p -o enc5 in
stderr 'passphrase'
! age --batch -e -R recipients.txt -o in in
stderr 'must be different'
! age --batch -e -R recipients.txt -o enc6
stderr 'input directory'

-- planted.age --
do-not-overwrite-this-file
